name: Sill Line, Instrumented
tagline: Lit Sill Line with only its pictures redrawn: Status opens on an instrument panel (a named lamp board beside a moving-coil spend meter), every state lamp is one family of six signals with one meaning each, and the greeting's airglow is a phosphor halftone.
concept: This is Lit Sill Line with its colours, type and layout left alone and three graphics redrawn as the dice rolled them. Status now opens on one thin graphite faceplate with two lit windows that answer the page's own question in order. The first is a lamp board with every lamp named, for 'is it working'. The second is a moving-coil spend meter whose scale is the lineage's line bent into an arc, for 'what is it costing'. Every lamp that says how something stands is now one family of six signals, each with one meaning, and only the working lamp gives off light. One surface, the greeting, carries a texture: its airglow off the lit run is now a halftone of phosphor dots.
companions:
These are the parent's, unchanged:
- Ink (#182536 plates with a #86a9cc cap) is what the family wrote.
- Steel is the board: #58697a rails and #a7c4d8 links. #a7c4d8 is now also the waiting dot and the printed cost bars.
- Pewter #7a8590 is the ring (off or idle) and the dashed socket (not set up).
- Amber #ffb850 means only 'needs a look': the upright bar (on Status, Settings, Worth a look and both To do rails), the late words and the setup edge.
- Red #ff6b6b means only 'stopped': the block.
- Sage #86d9a6 is 'now' and done.
- #6dff9c lights only the working lamp, the meter's needle and its lit run, the mark, 'planning', Send, the box, focus and the tubes.

On the glass, the dot, ring and socket take the tube's dim strength, and the bar stays amber, so 'needs a look' reads the same on glass and on the boards. Past spending (the cost table's strip bars) is printed steel on a dark well, never light.
decisions: Rolled: an instrument panel (major), one family of small signals (minor), and a faint texture on one surface (minor). Nothing else of the parent changed. The layout moved only where a picture needed room: Status's instrument row, and the notice on the spending settings page, which now stands beside a small copy of the meter.

The panel follows the lede, 'Is it working, and what is it costing?', in its order. The lamp window is on the left and flexible (13 named signals). The meter window on the right is 22.5rem. Both sit in one 3px graphite case with a 5px strip of case between them and one power lamp. The legend is printed along the foot of the case under the lamps it explains, with 'Change the limit' at its right end, under the meter it changes.

The meter is the lineage's line bent into an arc: a terminus ring at 0, ticks every 5% (long at each quarter), a hatched caution band from 75%, and a T buffer at the limit. The needle has a hot core and the tube's two-layer halo, with a lit run along the scale from 0 to today. Main round 12 faulted a needle resting at zero in stills; this answers it three ways. The limit is on the scale as the buffer. A bug on the rim marks a usual day (the last 30 days' dollars over 30), written under it as 'A usual day: $0.04'. And the figure is printed large under the pivot. The drawing is fixed (src/dial_geometry.py). Only the needle, the run and the bug move, by rotate() about the pivot and a dash on pathLength 100, so the template needs no trig. It is one macro, spend_dial in templates/_ui.html, shared by Status and settings/spending.html. Near the limit only the meter's window re-lights amber, and past it red; this was checked in a test render at $1.60 and $2.40.

Every lamp on the glass is named under its signal: Chat, Digest, Lookups, Fallback; Claude, OpenAI, Gemini, Telegram; Calendar, Weather, Web, Digest, Sign-in. Names of things that are not working are at the dim strength, and 'needs a look' is amber. Each string stays one 44px link to its board and goes inverse when pointed at. A screen reader hears each name with its state ('Chat working,'). This answers the round-2 lenses that asked for the glass lamps to be named.

One meaning each. The parent had two drawings for 'partly working' and 'needs a look' (a half-amber lamp and an amber dot); here they are one signal, the upright amber bar. Status's 'This page' row, which still uses the installer's password, now shows that bar rather than a working lamp. That matches what Settings already said, and interaction asked for it in round 2. The tally is now 5 working, 1 needs a look, 1 waiting, 2 off, 4 not set up, 0 stopped. The board heads now count signals, so 'Connected to' says 1 of 5 on the glass and on the board; the parent's board said 2 of 5.

The signals are real assets on one 16-unit grid (static/sig-lamp, -dot, -ring, -socket, -bar and -block .svg). Five are masks filled with their one colour, so no glow can leak onto them. The lamp is a jewelled lens (a radial core and a lens glint) with a drop-shadow halo that follows the lens. The family reaches the lamp board, the legend, the three boards, Settings, Worth a look, the Status key in the bar, and To do's timetable on Home and on its own page. There a late task is the amber bar on the rail, one due later is a steel dot waiting for its time, and one with no time is a pewter ring.

Working lamps burn steady: in a signal box a steady lamp is normal. The base sheet's breathing of every working lamp on Status and Settings is therefore off, which also stops the harness catching them half-dimmed. The zero rows the judges asked to drop or dim are dimmed ('0 stopped' in dim ink at weight 400) and kept, because the legend has to show every signal once.

The halftone is drawn at the page's own pixel size, so its dots stay round at any width (src/halftone.py writes static/halftone-sill.svg and a portrait halftone-gutter.svg for the phone's rail). It is a 45-degree screen at a 7px pitch. Each dot's radius is the airglow's strength: 2.1px over the lit run, falling off over about 60px upward and gone within 50px past the first stop, so the dates on the sill stay clean. It replaces the parent's whisper of scanlines on the greeting, so that surface carries one texture. The glass keeps its own scanlines (E14), as before.

Further down Status, the 'By kind of call' table gains a column of printed steel strip bars, ruled at the quarters, beside its figures, and 'Worth a look' uses the amber bar on its rail. These are matte because they are past data.

Built as the parent was: src/build.py themes today's stylesheet and appends the lineage's sources plus this mutant's src/instruments.css into variants/t3-track-mut/sheet.css (164K). More contrast drops the new halos. Forced colours draws every signal and the dial in CanvasText and hides the halftone. Reduced motion hides the roll in each window.
title: What are we *planning*? A dice mutant keeps its parent's words, so this is Lit Sill Line's title. It is the household's own present tense: it asks what the family has on the go and invites them to tell Vera, and the lit line of plans the question stands on answers it directly below. The lit word is the job, not the motif. It avoids 'next', which the tube's NEXT UP already claims, and 'shall', which the judges found stiff. It holds one line on the desktop and on a phone. As the box's label, it tells a first-time user what the box is for.

name: Departures, Hung
tagline: Departures, Posted set again: its roundels, ticks, rings, lamps and numbers hung in the margin so every page reads from one text edge, a condensed sign face and a humanist voice face in place of Archivo's three widths, and the family's chat bubbles back to plain slate.
concept: This is the parent's station after dark, typeset by someone who hangs their punctuation. Each page reads from one clean left edge, shared by the title, lede, controls, table, rules and rows. The markers all stand outside that edge in the margin, each column's on one centre line: the page roundel, the section roundels, the ticks, the kind rings, the Status lamps, the idea and task numbers, the warning sign, the settings rail and the opening quote of each way to start. Two faces now split the work. Barlow Condensed posts the signs and figures, and Red Hat Text speaks. The phosphor light stays exactly where the parent put it.
companions: All the companion roles are the parent's except one. Steel (pewter #9aa8a8 and the rails) is the metal: rules, leaders, rings, chevrons, the quotation marks around the ways to start, and "you are here". Each section's own colour (Ideas lilac, Plans sky, To do teal, Wishes pink) appears only in its roundel, the short lead under each head, the 2px cap under "here" and the kind rings. Steel-denim #a3b9d6 is used for links only. Bone is kept for the family's initials, amber only for late and "needs a look", and ink is a warm bone-white. The dice roll took the companion out of the family's chat bubbles: their 2px steel-denim spine is gone, and they are the quiet default, a slate plate in the card edge (the newest one keeps its phosphor glow).
decisions: COLOUR ROLL (take the companion out where it is weakest): I chose the family bubbles' 2px steel-denim spine. The judges had named it (the only non-green in a 96% green Chat was 'thin steel-denim edges... nearly neutral'), and it also broke the parent's own rule that denim is a link and nothing else. It goes back to the quiet default: bubble-them slate with the card edge, the newest stop's glow kept. I also weighed bone initials and steel labels. Bone is so close to ink that removing it would change nothing visible. Steel labels tie the labels to the rails, so they are doing a job.

TYPE ROLL (a new pairing, each face with one job): Barlow Condensed is the SIGN, what the station posts. That covers page names, section signs, the bar's places, the phone tab bar, the settings directory and rail, her line's name, labels over fields and columns, and every stand-alone figure (margin times, dates, counts, #ids, drive times, spend), in true tabular figures. Red Hat Text is the VOICE, what is said or done: her question, messages, the names of ideas, tasks and plans, every sentence, and the controls. VT323 stays on the glass as its one pre-existing job (the phosphor kit).

Why this pair: Barlow comes from the DIN road- and rail-sign lineage, which suits the station. Red Hat Text is humanist and warm, and different enough from Barlow to pair. Every other design this round is Plex, Archivo or DM, and serif titles have lost six times, so I avoided both.

The scale is written out as steps. The sign runs one step larger than the voice at every rank so the two read at one size: 3.25rem page name, 2.625 question (the largest words on Home), 2.25 figure, 1.625 sign, then 1.1875 / 1.0625 / 1 / 0.9375 / 0.875. The Ideas column heads and the month weekdays moved from tracked capitals to sentence case (a type fix the judges asked for). No text is smaller than 13px.

STRUCTURE ROLL (quotes and bullets hung outside the text edge), carried through every page. Page roundels hang in a margin that is one roundel wider on each side, so the measure inside is unchanged. Crumb arrows hang, and the Ideas #numbers hang right-aligned in the page margin. Status sign marks and lamps hang in the plates' margins on one centre line, and the in-order rail follows them. Settings directory rings hang in the board's margin. The General page's rail hangs straight down from the page roundel.

On Home, section roundels, To do ticks, the Lately added and Something-to-eat rings, and the notice's warning sign all hang. Her name moved onto the box's edge. Rules and enamel leads now start under the words, so the markers stand clear of them. The hover afterglow now starts at the margin and lights the hung ring.

Home's main keeps a gutter only on the left for the hung marks, and the three columns were rebalanced (0.78 / 1.2 / 1.36fr) so the departures board shows every destination whole and Send stays on its row.

name: Pocket Diary, Lit
tagline: Pocket Diary with the tube’s light back where the machine speaks: Vera’s words, times and readouts glow, the family’s stay matte, and the one key to press is lit from within.
concept: This is Pocket Diary with one rule added, drawn on every page: what the machine says gives off light, at the tube's own strengths, and what the family wrote stays matte and sharp. Her lines in Chat are now small screens: dark glass, a phosphor rim with a bloom, and her words in a pale phosphor with a soft halo. Her prompt in the box glows like a prompt on the glass, and every clock time, drive and 'Working' the machine reads out is dim-lit. The one key to press on each page is lit from within, and it pools light on the desk under it. It should feel like the parent's calm slate diary with the handheld's screen switched on behind the machine's words, so light marks who is speaking and where to press, never a wash across the page.
companions: No new colours. The parent's companions keep their jobs: bone headings #dcd8cb, denim links and the family's bubble edge #9db6d6, steel lines #4b5963, amber #eaa85d for late and needs a look, and the section colours on their tiles and caps. The only new tones are mixes of the exact #6dff9c, at the tube's strengths. Soft is 24% phosphor into cream (#c6f0d2-ish), for her words. Dim is the kit's 64% into green-black (#48aa68), for readouts and her prompt. Bright is the full phosphor under E1's halo, for now, live things and the key. Her bubbles sit on tube glass (#0c1912 to #07100b). The family's bubbles stay slate #1a2127 with the denim edge, so mine-versus-hers reads as lit glass against matte slate.

The changes are in variants/t3-pocket-mut/sheet.css only: the base key rules, a new 'Lit' section before Motion, and lines added to the more-contrast and forced-colours blocks.

Her words are in soft phosphor under a wide halo with no tight core: 0.5em at 42% and 1.4em at 16%. I checked at 3x that the stems stay sharp, since the Tube Lit mutant was faulted for soft stems. Her name is full phosphor and her stamps are dim-lit. The family's bubbles, names and stamps have no shadow at all.

'4 open' stays ink, because the parent's key keeps green for now or working.

Her prompt in the box ('Plans for the weekend…' on Home, 'Message Vera' in Chat) is the machine speaking, so it is dim-lit like a prompt on the glass. What the family types over it is ink. name: Switchboard, Squared
tagline: Switchboard, Patched as the dice squared it: every window of glass, lamp, LED and radar blip cut as a square cell, the wiring back to quiet graphite hairlines, and nothing faux in the type, so the heads, names and figures the parent asked to be condensed are now set in the true IBM Plex Sans Condensed.
concept: This is the videotex switchboard with the square made its one shape. A videotex page is built from square character cells, so here the glass windows, the lamps, the LEDs on "here", the power lights and the radar's blips are square as well, and every icon's line ends and joints are cut square. The panel's wiring goes back to plain graphite, so the frames and rules recede and the colour stays in what it counts. The type draws only the cuts that exist. It should feel like a calmer, crisper switchboard: square, matte and exact, with light only where the machine is live.
companions: Graphite does the wiring now: every cell frame, the rules between rows and the dotted leaders use card-edge #262e2a, line #232a26 and line-2 #323a36. They are no longer 30-45% mixes of each section's colour. The section circuits stay low-chroma but live only where they carry meaning: in the figures, icons, links and kind words. Those are periwinkle #acadea for Ideas, sky #9ccdf8 for Plans and the day numerals, sea #83d5d4 for To do and heather #cda2bf for Wishes. Bone #cdc6b5 goes to the household pages (Home, Vera, Status, Settings): their counts, icons and links. Steel marks "here": a #56697b block with a #a9c4d8 cap, and the waiting lamp in #93b4c8. The off lamp is pewter #8794a2. Clay #a99389 is for restaurants. Amber #eaa76b means only "needs a look" and late. #6dff9c stays exact: the mark, Send, "plan", focus, the lit squares and the tubes.
decisions: COLOUR roll (the companion leaves one role, which goes back to its quiet default): I took the section colour out of the WIRING, that is the frames, the rules between rows, the column-head rules and the dotted leaders. On Home those frames sampled (71,91,101) for Plans, (76,81,97) for Ideas and (86,89,81) for the household. That is where the companion was weakest. A 1px hairline at 30% does not read as 'Plans'. It only made the boxes louder, and it was the skeptic's fault with the parent ('30% coloured box frames make it wiry and busy; frames plus leaders make a wireframe'). They are now graphite: card-edge, line and line-2. The companion keeps its strong roles, the big sky day numerals, the counts, the icons and the links. The setup line keeps its amber leader, because amber is the signal, not the companion.

STRUCTURE roll (everything square or everything round): I chose SQUARE. The parent was already square in everything the family owns, so the roll lands on the machine, the last round things. The glass is now cut square in the plate: the Home terminal, the chat composer, every head tube, sign-in and 404. The tube's curve is drawn by its own light: the inset vignette was deepened to 40px/0.74, and the corner falloff to 0.66 black from 52%. Lamps are indicator squares that keep the shape code: on is a 10px lit square with a white-hot centre and two halos; waiting is a small steel square; off is a hollow pewter square; needs a look is the square-ended amber bar. The LEDs on the current key and menu, the power lights, the next plan's lamp and the error and chosen marks are squares too. In the markup (_ui.html), the radar's hub, blips, pings and lit marks are now square rects, so a plan on the scope is a lit pixel. The icons get stroke-linecap square and linejoin miter, and the rounded rects in the sprite lose their rx, so the mark, the calendar, the gift and the mic are square-cornered. The checkbox tick and the sign-in face are square-ended. The select's checkmark becomes a square, and bullets are square.

The one exception is the radar scope. Its circle is its scale (rings at a week, two and four, or at 15 min, 45 min and 2 h), not a corner. Square rings would misplace every blip on the diagonals, so the scope keeps its disc while its marks go square. The radio-button rule keeps its round drawing: a round radio is what tells it from a checkbox, and no page uses one.

TYPE roll (font-synthesis off everywhere): the parent already had font-synthesis: none on body, and a probe of every element found nothing faux drawn (no VT323 above 400, no synthetic italic). So the literal change was already in place, except on html and head. Now it is on :root, *, the pseudo-elements, ::placeholder, ::marker, the form controls and svg text. To make the roll's rule visible, I carried it through: only cuts a type designer drew appear. The parent's sheet asked for 'condensed' or 'semi-condensed' IBM Plex Sans in 33 places: page titles, cell heads, row and item names, counts, the day numerals, the month's days, sign-in and 404. Plex Sans has no such width, so the browser had silently set them all at normal width. They now use the true cut, IBM Plex Sans Condensed 400/500/600, through one --cond token. Plex Sans Condensed sits about where semi-condensed would, so it is the nearest real cut for both requests. This follows the parent's own written scale ('32 condensed 600: a page's name'), which had never rendered as written.

Everything else is the parent's, unchanged: the palette tokens, glow, screenGlow and topGlow at 1.0, the sommaire Home, the lit radar and day-numeral pair, the setup service line, the racks, the words and the title. The changes sit in one part (tools/parts/g_mutant.css) plus the condensed swap in the parts, the square rects in templates/_ui.html and the rx removed in static/icons.svg, so the judges can trace each one.

name: Diary in Ink
tagline: The family's pocket diary in two hands. The printed days and the machine's phosphor run on one steel line of time. The family's own words, fields and names are in blue-black ink, and how far off each thing is gets pencilled in the margin.
concept: Pocket Diary had the print of a diary and none of the handwriting. Diary in Ink adds the family's hand in two materials, each with one job. Blue-black ink is the solid for what the family writes and who a thing is for. Graphite pencil, set in Victor Mono italic, says how far off something is, and turns amber when it is late. The machine keeps its phosphor, now with the tube's full halo on the one lit word and the Now plates. Setup shrinks to one amber stop on the steel line, which frees the shelf so To do stands beside the box.
companions: Ink is low-chroma blue-black. Wells are #0c131b with a #4a6585 edge, and tags are #152131 with a #2a3c55 edge. A chat slip is a larger solid, so it is nearer slate (#131a22 with a #26303b edge), and its blue-black lives in the 2px #7f9cbf cap and the speaker's square. Ink goes on fields, the family's chat slips and the who-tags (To do, Home's To do and Later, the kids' wishes, the Ideas table), and is never a text colour or a row fill. Graphite #aab2ae, in pencil, is only for how far off: Home's Coming up and To do, the Plans agenda and list, and the To do page. Amber #eaa85d is only for late or 'needs a look'. That means the setup stop's node, figure and turn-in; the late pencil notes and their spine nodes (with a light scrawl on the To do page only); the '3 late' link; and the sign-in lamps. Everything else is as in the parent: denim #9db6d6 links, underlined; steel lines; bone heads; slate; and #6dff9c where something is now or live.
decisions: Ink (L004, Kitchen Clock) is rebuilt as a material, not a colour: it covers fields, the family's chat slips and who-tags. The well edge is #4a6585 (3.1:1) rather than the brief's #2b3d52, so fields keep the 3:1 rule for edges. Focus stays E4's phosphor edge, ring and bloom, so the family writes in ink and the machine lights it.

In this revision the chat slips have their own, slate-leaning ink (#131a22, edge #26303b), because a large slip in full ink read as navy on a phone. The small tags and the wells keep the full blue-black.

Pencil (L164, Glow Ink Zine): Victor Mono italic 400 at 15px in graphite, with no tracking. It is the one script, with one job, how far off. 'today' stays the machine's word, in Plex Sans 600 phosphor with E1.
Late is said in one place: the amber pencil note, plus the 6px spine node on To do. The time, the month and weekday and the tick go back to steel and ink-2.

Setup is one stop on the line (L042, Single Quote): an 8px amber node and an amber turn-in, then '3 steps to finish setting up · Next: Choose your own password', with a 'See all 3' fold. On a phone the fold becomes a chevron beside the count. Its words stay for screen readers, so the stop is two lines.

Home is restacked: To do opens the shelf level with the box's top, unboxed on its own short steel line, with the lit Now line between late and the rest. On wide screens the shelf is now sticky and spans both of Home's rows, so it stays beside the line as the page scrolls.

Light: the question's 'plan' carries the tube's layered halo (1px, 6px, 18px and the wide E1 bloom). The Now plates on Home, on the shelf and on To do carry the same layered text halo with a second, wider afterglow. Palette glow, screenGlow and topGlow are all 1.0.
Plans: Earlier and Later sit 8px above the month tube, spanning its exact width as its own controls.

Typesetting: the four voices, one job each, are stated in the sheet's header, plus VT323 on glass only. On the shelf the who-tag and the pencil note share a baseline under the title. On the phone the question is set at 30px.
title: What should we *plan*? — It is kept from the last round, as the critic asked. 'Plan' is the family's job with Vera (weekends, outings, the calendar, things to do), it asks for something to be told, it fits one line on a phone, and it keeps the lineage's question form with one lit key word.

name: Lit Manual, Relit Rails
tagline: The family's operator manual with its tubes switched back on: every figure touches its rows, one lit NOW per list, and the light only where the machine is live.
concept: Railed's one rule, kept and now held on every page: a figure touches its rows, and every list in time hangs from a rail with a lit NOW. The monitors are real phosphor tubes again: Home's countdown, the round Plans and Status gauges, the radar and the machine. Anything live smaller than 1.2rem is a lamp, white-hot at the core and breathing in its halo. It feels like a calm, well-set technical manual on green-black and bone, lit only where the machine is live.
companions: Bone ink (#dcd8ca, headings #e8e2d0) carries the reading on green-black. Blueprint (#6f88b3, #9fb4d6) is only in the drawings' lines and prose links; the sheet is green-black (#0e1513), so blue never fills an area. Sky (--when, now #9db6cf, one step more chroma) is time's ink, always split from a dim weekday: rail dates, the chat's date rule and its tick across the lanes, the month's week ranges, and the Plans 'Next' line. Clay (#c79071) is only for the Restaurant and Something to eat squares. Amber (#f1af64) is spent only on what needs a look: late rows' 3px edge and words, '3 late' in To do's head link and the Late key's count, the setup rings, Settings' ring 8, Status's 'This page' lamp, port and words, and the one caution line on slate. Steel (#a9c4d8 cap on a low tint) marks 'here' in the bar, tabs, keys and the settings nav. The seasonal kind is brick #de6a55, so it stays apart from clay.
decisions: Tokens. The sheet is green-black #0e1513 with edge #24302c. The grid alpha is 0.06/0.03 with a 24px fine grid. --when is time's ink and --clay is food's. --t-plate (22/28) sets Home's plate heads, so Home reads 52 > 22 > 16. Every eyebrow, legend and column head uses --t-label (14px, sentence case), and drawing words are 13px mono.

Phosphor. Every NOW is a 2px #6dff9c line under two halos, its node a lamp with a #e4fff0 core, and its word 'Now' at 14px in E1. The monitors carry the kit's glass: three strengths, a 0.35px blur, 1-in-3 scanlines, a sheen, corners falling to #000, and a breathing power lamp. 'plan' keeps E1. The E7 pool sits under Send only.

Lamps under 1.2rem: To do's next due (in both figures now), the newest chat arrow's head (and on the phone, a lamp beside the newest line's speaker), the wiring's model and ports, the form anatomy's live field, and the month's this-week stop. This revision makes every one breathe in its halo, never in its core. The old opacity breathe left the NOW node reading grey.
Row afterglow: pointing at a row lights its stop in 0.12s and fades over 1.2s, with a 2px phosphor edge on that row's stretch of the rail.

Home: the title comes first, then the box and Send, with the countdown tube at right. The tube shows 'Next in 2 days' (bright, with the CRT cursor), '13:00 Sun 4 Oct' and '3 more on the rail ↓'. Below 48rem it also prints the plan's name. Coming up's sheet now opens on the lit NOW node, level with To do's first rule. To do on Home keeps a short lit 'Now' tick, with one head link: 'All 4 · 3 late →'.

Chat: the sequence diagram is drawn in each message's own row, its arrows at their speaker lines. The lane heads have a row of their own and stick to the top of the figure column. A sky tick runs across the lanes for each day. A quiet dotted run joins each arrow to the sheet's edge, and the lifelines end under the last arrow.

Plans: Gauged Manual's round tube is relit, reading 'Next in / 2 days / then 3 more', with each line set once. On Month, the month's head ('October 2026', Earlier, Later) moved into the title plate. It sits under the tabs and a one-line 'Next  Oaks Park roller rink  Sun 4 Oct · 13:00', right over the grid it heads. Each week's range is centred on its stop, and a filled stop means a week with plans. 'weekend free' is written in words. Past empty weeks fold behind a break mark. NOW leaves this week's lamp level with it and stops at the grid's edge, and today's lit outline carries it on.

The route has no 'late' status, so the key sends status=open&cut=late and the template keeps the late rows; a real build would add the status to routes.tasks. The tally and the rail share one shape language: a task is a round counter, no date is a dashed square, and the next due is a lamp. Both legends are the same 14px HTML key.

Sign-in and 404: the figure-column hairline now runs the full height of main, as on every other page.

firstDraft.name: Switchboard, Patched Through
firstDraft.concept: Home is still the videotex sommaire, the map of the whole service. Now the board also patches calls through. Pointing at a way to start lights the jack of the page its message usually lands on, so the box, the keys and the map read as one circuit. The wireframe of coloured frames is gone. Each panel is matte graphite with one teletext cap of separated blocks. The inner pages' wide green head tubes are cut down to a one-line Row 0 service line, and phosphor light is kept for the glass, the lamps, Send and the next plan's numeral. It should feel like a calm graphite switchboard where light means something is live or about to be connected.
